subject: SLA Evidence & Measurement — Audit Playbook (proposal)
messages:

Subject: RFP question: evidence & measurement for availability/latency

Sergio —

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the RFP. A couple of follow-ups from our side: for the availability / latency sections we need a concise description of how Redwood measures these SLOs, what evidence (raw vs aggregated) you will provide during an audit, the retention windows for telemetry, and the exact formula you use to calculate service credits.

Two specific asks from procurement and engineering:
- Example Datadog/PromQL queries we can run to validate SLOs from our monitoring side.
- How you account for cache effects (e.g., prefix cache hits), model fallbacks, and synthetic probe vs production-data discrepancies when computing latency percentiles.

Can you send a short playbook we can include in the RFP appendix? We prefer something that is clear enough to hand to our auditors.

Thanks,
Sarah

Sr. Procurement Manager, Acme Corporation
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme.com>
Cc: dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-12 13:42 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP question: evidence & measurement for availability/latency

Sarah —

Appreciate the clarity. I put together a short "SLA Audit Playbook" (attached) but key points summarized below so you can review quickly:

1) Measurement surfaces
- Production telemetry: per-request traces and per-token timing collected at the ingress and post-kernel stages.
- Synthetic probes: active probes (1-min cadence by default) from multiple regions to validate egress/network paths and cold-start behavior.
- Aggregates: 1m/5m aggregates for latency percentiles and availability windows used for SLA calculations.

2) Attribution & normalization
- Attribution buckets: we label each request with routing tier (hosted/dedicated/private), model variant, and cache status (prefix cache hit/miss, KV cache warmed).
- Cache normalization: when computing customer-visible p50/p95/p99 we exclude synthetic probe results and apply a weighted adjustment for prefix cache hit-rate delta. The playbook documents the exact weighting heuristic (example: normalized_latency = observed_latency * (1 - w*cache_hit_rate) where w is tuned by model class).

3) Exclusions & force-majors
- Planned maintenance windows, upstream cloud provider incidents (>99.9% external responsibility), and customer-induced misconfigurations are excluded.
- We publish a rolling list of permitted maintenance windows; unannounced platform incidents are included in measurement.

4) Sample retention & evidence types
- Aggregated SLO metrics: retained 365 days (CSV/Parquet export available).
- Raw trace sub-samples (1:100 by default): retained 90 days. Full raw traces available for 30-day audit requests on signed NDA.

5) Credit calculation (summary)
- Credits are calculated monthly: credit = min(max( (SLO_target - observed_SLO) / SLO_target, 0), 1) * monthly_service_fee * credit_multiplier
- For partial degradations (e.g., elevated p99 but p95 within target) we apply a weighted penalty function that maps percentile regressions to a single availability delta. Details in section 3 of the attached.

6) Evidence package delivered on request
- Aggregated timeseries (CSV), Datadog query strings, sample raw traces (redacted), event timelines combining synthetic probe and production telemetry, and our internal incident timeline.

I attached the playbook and a short sample of Datadog queries. Kimberly / Dev — flag anything missing at a high level.

If this looks OK I can turn it into an RFP appendix and include the exact Datadog snippets as part of the deliverable.

— Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Director, Reliability & Inference, Redwood Inference

Quick internal notes before we send final:
- Retention: confirm legal ok with 365d aggregates + 90d raw sample. Procurement sometimes wants 2 years aggregated. If Acme pushes, we should include an optional paid extension.
- Sampling: 1:100 raw traces is fine but we should provide a deterministic seed window for audits so their auditors can reproduce sampling boundaries.
- Cache weighting: the proposed linear weight is ok for most models but for very short prompts (<= 32 tokens) the prefix cache has outsized effect. We should add a short appendix explaining small-prompt adjustment.
- PII: any raw traces provided for audit must be redacted and vetted by legal.

I can draft the appendix on retention options and seeded sampling.

—Kimberly
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-13 09:10 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP question: evidence & measurement for availability/latency

Thanks Kim — noted. Responses to your points and additions for the RFP appendix:

- Retention tiers:
  * Standard: aggregates 365d, raw sub-samples 90d (included).
  * Extended: aggregates 2y, raw sub-samples 1y (paid add-on).

- Deterministic sampling: we can expose audit-seed tokens (hash of minute-window + account id) so auditors can reproduce which traces were sampled. Include a short reproducibility script in the playbook.

- Small-prompt adjustment: add a bounded adjustment factor (alpha) for requests <=32 tokens. Alpha scales linearly from 0.15 to 0.03 across [1,32] tokens — details in the playbook.

- Redaction workflow: legal will run a redaction pass on any raw trace exports; metadata and aggregates are safe to share immediately.

Artifacts live in the shared drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-sla-artifacts and I added sample Datadog queries and a CSV of retention options. HubSpot ticket HS-23891 created to track follow-up.

I'll send the finalized appendix to Acme this afternoon.

— Sergio

Thanks for the detail, Sergio — this is helpful. Two follow-ups from our SREs:

1) Credit allocation for partial degradations — can you provide a concrete worked example mapping elevated p99 to credit percentage over a monthly billing cycle? Our auditors prefer a spreadsheet with a few scenarios.

2) Cache normalization — the linear weight helps but our concern is that services with different prompt-length distributions get different effective SLOs. We want a normalization approach that is prompt-length-aware and easy to validate from exported aggregates.

If you can drop the sample Datadog queries and a worked credit spreadsheet, that should be sufficient for our auditors to move to legal.

Regards,
Sarah
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-14 10:25 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP question: evidence & measurement for availability/latency

Sarah —

Attached are: (1) sample-datadog-queries.txt (includes p50/p95/p99 queries and a prompt-length breakout), and (2) a worked spreadsheet embedded in the playbook showing three scenarios. Quick example from the spreadsheet:

- Monthly hours = 24 * 30 = 720
- Observed_availability = 99.45% (i.e., 3.96 hours of degraded/unavailable time)
- SLO_target = 99.9%
- Availability_delta = SLO_target - Observed_availability = 0.45%
- Credit = Availability_delta / SLO_target * monthly_service_fee
  e.g., if monthly_service_fee = $50,000 -> Credit = 0.0045 / 0.999 * 50,000 ≈ $225.

For percentile-driven regressions we calculate a single-equivalent availability delta by mapping percentile deltas to a cost function (see section 3). We also provide an optional per-prompt-length normalization export (CSV) so you can reproduce the adjustments: the export contains counts and median latencies per length-bucket (1-16, 17-32, 33-64, 65+).

Next steps: if this is acceptable, confirm by EOD Friday and we'll attach the RFP appendix and the spreadsheet in the formal RFP response. If Acme wants longer retention or on-site audit, we can include pricing options.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if your SREs want to walk through the queries.

— Sergio
